name: Alacritty
summary: A Rust terminal emulator whose PTY event loop feeds a reusable terminal parser/grid, while a platform window, GPU renderer, input/clipboard layer, and optional IPC/configuration paths provide host integration.
scope: terminal parser, grid, scrollback, and modes
keyboard, mouse, selection, and clipboard input

features.name: PTY and I/O event loop
features.description: Alacritty's PTY reader thread polls the child endpoint, feeds its parser while holding the terminal lock, queues input writes, and emits application wakeups. The read loop caps bytes processed while locked to avoid monopolizing terminal state; child-exit and resize transitions are handled alongside I/O readiness.
benefits: Keeps child I/O and terminal parsing independently testable
Uses an event-driven path for output and resize/exit notifications
costs: PTY and platform process behavior remain OS-specific
Output bursts can pressure queues and redraw scheduling

features.name: Terminal parser and grid state
features.description: The terminal crate parses control sequences into terminal actions and maintains a grid, scrollback, cursor, modes, selection, and vi-style navigation state.
benefits: Provides deterministic terminal-state tests and a reusable terminal crate
Separates protocol state from the window frontend
costs: Grid and scrollback memory scale with configured history
Terminal protocol state has many compatibility-sensitive modes

features.name: Window and renderer boundary
features.description: Alacritty maps terminal content and damage into a platform window and GPU renderer, with font rasterization, glyph caching, resize, and presentation handled around the terminal state.
benefits: Keeps window-system and renderer code outside the terminal crate
costs: GPU drivers, window systems, and font stacks vary by platform
Glyph caches and high-resolution surfaces consume resources

features.name: Keyboard, mouse, selection, and clipboard input
features.description: Alacritty converts platform window events into keyboard and mouse actions, terminal bytes, selection changes, and clipboard operations according to configurable bindings and modes.
benefits: Makes input policy configurable without changing PTY semantics
Supports selection and clipboard as explicit terminal interactions
costs: Binding precedence and terminal application modes can surprise users
Clipboard access crosses the GUI and host-service boundary

features.name: IPC, configuration, and process resource boundary
features.description: On Unix, Alacritty's IPC listener decodes JSON CreateWindow, Config, and GetConfig messages and posts them into the GUI event loop. These controls are distinct from terminal-program OSC 52 clipboard requests: the terminal core defaults to OnlyCopy, accepting clipboard writes but rejecting reads. Scrollback configuration separately caps retained history at 100,000 lines at this revision.
benefits: Enables multi-window automation and configuration reload workflows
Keeps optional control paths outside normal terminal byte processing
costs: Control endpoints and inherited environment affect authority
Configuration changes can alter input, window, and child-process behavior

assumptions: Resources have explicit creation and teardown points

assumptions: Bindings and terminal modes select transitions
